app.notes:
### Changed

- **A hidden settings panel stays hidden.** Clicking a rail item that has a dot (say, a firmware update for your board) no longer opens the panel you hid: the dot shows on the panel's show button and on the section, and when you show the panel it opens at that section. Clicking the item of the page you're on still shows or hides its panel, the same in the narrow window's drawer.
- **Nothing to unfold in the readouts.** Games → This computer always shows the HDR checklist (one short line when everything passes, a problem highlighted); Controller info shows Sony's update steps while a newer official firmware is out; a game's Setup shows its passed checks and the Controller not detected mark, and DualSense support shows what the tiers mean; HDR's Set it up yourself is a short numbered list; the Windows USB repair shows the exact script it runs. All compact.
- **Feedback is its own section on a game's page.** What you noticed (triggers work, vibration feels weak…) moved out of DualSense support into a Feedback section in the settings panel, with the number ticked as its status. Your ticks are kept.
- **Tidier clean-up.** The Proton update check during a Games scan no longer leaves a 5-second timer behind once the answer is in; the watcher that follows the desktop's accent color is stopped when the app quits; and the Developer card's HDR test releases its graphics device when it closes (dev builds).
- **Less work behind the Games grid, the Pico 2 W log and the HDR glow.** A big Games library no longer redraws every cover tile each time the page updates (only a tile whose game changed); the Pico 2 W page's log no longer redraws its rows ten times a second with the live screen (only when a line is added); and with HDR lighting on, dragging the window's edge no longer rebuilds the full-size glow mask on every frame (the glow follows the drawing and is rebuilt once you let go). Looks the same.
- **A big game library scans without holding up the app (Linux).** The Games scan reads each game's Steam manifest, Heroic settings file and Lutris file in parallel before it looks at them, instead of one after another on the app's main thread; a Proton build's version file is read once however many games use it; Steam's per-game settings are looked up through one index instead of a search through thousands of entries per game; and the game details reuse the scan's reads. Same results, less waiting (and the tray and window stay responsive while it runs).
- **The OLED is the centerpiece of the Pico 2 W page again.** The page opens on the DS5 Dongle OLED Edition's screen, named as what it is (Waveshare Pico-OLED-1.3 · 1.3″ · 128 × 64 · SH1107), mirrored live and large, with what it's doing now beside it (brightness, on / dimmed / off, which of the 11 screens, redraws per second, frame) and the module's specs. They had ended up at the bottom of Diagnostics; they're in one place now, the OLED's, and the mirror's line under the picture is gone (it said the same). Below it in a narrow window. The dials and Diagnostics follow. All 7 languages.

### Added

- **Collapse all and Clear pins.** A small ⋮ at the top of every settings panel, the same on every page: Collapse all folds every section, pinned ones too (they stay pinned and open again next time); Clear pins unpins this page's sections. Works with the keyboard, in every language.
- **Lock the rail collapsed.** A small lock in the rail's bottom corner keeps the rail small, icons only, so it no longer opens when you point at it; click it again to unlock. Remembered across restarts.
- **Share your OLED.** A Share button beside the OLED's name on the Pico 2 W page saves exactly what the screen shows: **Save PNG** (1×, 4× or 8×, every OLED pixel a crisp square, with or without the board around it as the mirror draws it), **Copy** (the picture on the clipboard, ready to paste into Discord) and **Record GIF** (up to 10 seconds, a frame each time the picture changes, with a recording dot, Stop and Cancel). Files are saved where you pick in the system's save dialog; nothing is uploaded. It uses the frames the mirror already reads, and makes the file only when you ask, off the page's thread. Works with the simulated board too. All 7 languages.
- **KEY0 and KEY1 on the screen, like on the module.** Two keys beside the live screen, where they sit on the Waveshare board, level with the `>` and `<` the screen draws: click KEY0 for the next screen and KEY1 for the previous one; hold KEY1 for 1.5 s (a bar fills while you hold) to step the brightness, as on the board. Each key's tooltip says what it does on the screen shown; Space or Enter work the same from the keyboard. The press goes to your board (firmware with protocol 1.18), which treats it exactly like a finger on the key, the OLED wired or not; older firmware shows the keys with what to update. The simulated board (dev builds) moves through its screens the same way. All 7 languages.
- **Pick any Proton version for a game (Linux).** A game's page, Compatibility, lists every Proton and Wine build its launcher can run it with: Steam's compatibility tools (compatibilitytools.d and Valve's own Protons), Heroic's Wine and Proton builds, and Lutris's Wine versions, with the DualSense Proton build at the top as recommended and the one the game uses now marked. Picking another says what changes and which file, a running Steam, Heroic or Lutris is named as closed and reopened before anything is written, the old setting is backed up first, and Undo puts it back right there (or from the change history). Not shown on Windows or macOS, where games don't run through Proton. All 7 languages.
- **The controller buttons the screen uses, beside it.** R1, the directional buttons and △ ○ ✕ □ (Sony's glyphs) next to the live screen, so every OLED screen can be worked from the app: Settings (up / down pick, left / right change, △ saves; hold △ 2 s on Reset to defaults or Wipe all slots), Slots (pick, △ use, hold □ 1.5 s to forget), Lightbar (R1 mode, △ ○ ✕ □ save a favorite), Trigger Test (△ next effect) and Diagnostics (scroll). Click to press; hold to hold (a bar fills over the hold the screen needs). Each button's tooltip says what it does on the screen shown, and buttons a screen doesn't use are greyed out. Only the board's screen sees these presses: games never do (firmware with protocol 1.19; older firmware shows them with what to update). Settings, Slots and Diagnostics work without a controller; Lightbar and Trigger Test need one. Space or Enter work from the keyboard. The simulated board (dev builds) answers them on its Settings, Slots, Lightbar, Trigger Test and Diagnostics screens. All 7 languages.

### Fixed

- **Automatic update checks off now means nothing goes online at start.** With *Check for updates automatically* off, the Games page's check for a newer DualSense Proton still reached the update server at every start (the Games badge's background scan) and on every scan. It now follows the switch like the firmware checks: the app goes online only when you press a check button or Install. With the switch on, the Games scan shares the update check's one download of the feed instead of fetching its own each time (Linux).
- **Install right after Check now downloads exactly what you were shown, without asking the server again.** The firmware Install reuses the update feed the offer came from while it is fresh (under a minute), and checks an older offer against the feed as it is now.
- **Game colors aren't worked out again after every scan.** With the Glass look, each Games scan made the app decode every game's cover again to find its color; a color is now kept until the game's art file changes.
- **A game installed or updated while the app runs is seen as Playing (Windows).** The list of a game's programs was read once per session, so a game that was still installing, or whose update renamed its program, was never recognised as running until the app restarted. Changed game folders are read again (checked once a minute).
- **The tray icon recovers from a failed draw.** If the tray picture failed to load once, the icon stayed blank for the session; the next update now tries again.
- **Every error in your language.** Messages that came from the app's background process or from talking to your board were always in English: setting up USB access, the Windows USB repair, installing DualSense Proton (downloads, disk space), Undo, Game setup's scan, a game's launcher files, the controller's volume, board errors (another program at the same time, no answer in time, an incomplete answer, firmware too old for a feature), USB errors, and the dialog when the app can't start. They're all in the 7 languages now, saying what happened and what to do.
- **A damaged backup no longer vanishes from Change history.** Games → Change history left out a change whose backup couldn't be read, so its Undo disappeared without a word. It is listed now, with when it was made, saying it can't be undone here and which folder holds the backup (all 7 languages).
- **A firmware update that didn't start now says so.** If the new firmware won't start, your board goes back to BOOTSEL mode; the update used to keep waiting and then ask you to press the PS button. Now the app sees the board come back in BOOTSEL within seconds of the restart, says plainly that the firmware didn't start, and offers **Install again** right there (all 7 languages). First-time setup says the same when the installed firmware doesn't start. Developer card → Simulated board has a new failure to try it: "Image that won't start".
- **A damaged settings or library file no longer silently starts empty.** If settings.json, your game library (game profiles, button layouts, ratings and notes) or the app's stored lists (dismissed notices, pinned sections, the pairing slots' controllers, your controller's colors, unticked Games changes) can't be read in full, the app keeps everything that still reads, puts defaults only where something was damaged, saves a copy of the damaged file next to it (`settings.json.corrupt-<date>`, `game-library-2.json.corrupt-<date>`), and tells you once in a notice what happened, what was kept and where the copy is (all 7 languages). It used to move a damaged library aside and show an empty one with no word.
